items.text: Before selling your land, offer it first to your next of blood.
items.quote: he must make an offer to the next of Blood

work: Lex Custumaria, or A Treatise of Copy-hold Estates: Caps. IV, V and XXV
heading: CAP. IV. · Custom. What things are requisite to make a good Custom.

items.text: Offer your copyhold land to your nearest blood relative at the agreed price before selling it to a stranger.
items.quote: If any Copy-holder will sell his Land, and agree upon the Price, at the next Court the next of his Blood... may have the Land.

items.text: Let the widow hold the whole copyhold estate for her free bench or during her widowhood.
items.quote: the Wife shall have the whole for her free Bench

items.text: Appoint a successor to your copyhold estate, lest the land escheat to the lord.
items.quote: A Copy-holder ought to nominate his Successor, otherwise the Land shall Escheat.

items.text: When a copyholder leaves only daughters, give the eldest surviving daughter the estate for her life, after which it passes to the next male heir.
items.quote: the eldest shall have this for Life, and after her death it shall go to the next Heir Male of the Father

work: Lex Custumaria, or A Treatise of Copy-hold Estates: Caps. IV, V and XXV
heading: CAP. V. · Of Customs in respect of the Estate. … In respect of Discents.

items.text: When the father dies, let the youngest son inherit the copyhold as the custom requires.
items.citation: Lex Custumaria, Cap. V, In respect of Discents
items.quote: if he be first admitted to Bondland, and afterwards to Sookland, and of them dye seized, his youngest Son shall Inherit

items.text: When the youngest son dies childless, let the elder brother inherit as his heir, not the middle brother.
items.citation: Lex Custumaria, Cap. V, In respect of Discents
items.quote: The elder Brother shall have this as Heir to the youngest, and not the middle Brother
